### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`  _(via compactToolbar (literal, a string literal in sections))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe3fb6c5a44d6bf46024fd3d8a1864a8995b5553` — the merge of head `ca02fd3f89afbb29c51208859b7183818b5e5314` into base `76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe3fb6c5a44d6bf46024fd3d8a1864a8995b5553 && git checkout fe3fb6c5a44d6bf46024fd3d8a1864a8995b5553
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f ca02fd3f89afbb29c51208859b7183818b5e5314 && git checkout -B drift-repro 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f && git merge --no-ff ca02fd3f89afbb29c51208859b7183818b5e5314

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head ca02fd3f · 2026-11-24T06:35Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `ca02fd3f89afbb29c51208859b7183818b5e5314`
Card: #36353 (from contract review 7076152814 N2/N3 on #36339) · os-dev-report 7123443977 · surface amendment 7123463265. Contract review claimed on this head (7124084371) at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, face schema (`view.zod.ts`, `view.form.ts`); the record follows.

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` CLEAN, 13 items. Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36353`. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Checks at this head:** 60 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- **Governance:** NOT governed, 39 lines, most of them generated.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. `compactToolbar` stays `z.boolean().optional()`; only its `.describe()` string moves. No accept set changes.
- **Changeset:** spec and platform-objects at patch, both published with src moved. The prose is true sentence by sentence. The claim that the translated help texts keep their current wording is also true: only the en bundle is regenerated.
- **The describe against the renderer on this head** (`ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`):
  - on by default: true. `compactToolbar: schema.compactToolbar !== false` (:2718);
  - the compact toolbar draws no Refresh: true. The Refresh button sits behind `toolbarFlags.showRefresh && !toolbarFlags.compactToolbar` (:8125), and `showRefresh` is `ua?.refresh !== false` (:2710);
  - pull-to-refresh is unaffected: true. `usePullToRefresh` (:3680) reads neither key.
  It now matches the `userActions.refresh` describe from #36339.
- **Card "Done when":** all three lines met. The describe states the default and the absence of Refresh; the form hint equals the describe, as the existing pin requires; the docs and en bundle are regenerated; and the liveness note names the wide-toolbar scope with reader lines pinned to a measured sha (5c2e34cdb).
- **Scope:** inside the amended surface (7123463265).
- **Overlap:** the only conflict with #36802 is a generated one, in `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`; it resolves with `merge=os-regen`.

### Findings
Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.
- **N1 (nit):** the kept first sentence calls the compact toolbar "a single View settings popover", while the renderer's own comment and #36339 call it the Display toolbar or panel. Two names for one surface. The card did not ask for it, so leave it, or align it on a later text card.

### Landing notes
The area lands once this ACCEPT and a PASS contract-review record on this head are both in place. `Fixes #36353` closes the card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ca02fd3f89afbb29c51208859b7183818b5e5314`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/view.json

Inputs read: card #36353 with all five comments (triage 7076775316, unblock 7101079773, claim 7122783775, dev report 7123443977, claim amendment 7123463265), PR #36872 body, its 8-file list and the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The renderer was read at `origin/main` `0819cab13` and at the PR head; `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` is byte-identical on the two, so every line number below holds on both.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged, and the PR says so correctly. `compactToolbar` stays `z.boolean().optional()` at `view.zod.ts:3664`; only the `.describe()` string changes. No key, type, default, optionality or strictness moves, so every view that parsed before parses the same and nothing that was refused is now accepted.
- Public surface: the description text of one property changes, and with it the description in the generated JSON schema and the three regenerated reference pages. Text only. Right.
- `view.form.ts:109`: the `helpText` is the same string as the describe, character for character. The pin `view-form-composite-children.test.ts:97-101` asserts `helpText` equals the schema description for `compactToolbar`, and Test Core is green on this head. Right.
- `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts`: one `helpText` line, the same string. It is generated from the form hint, and its package is in the changeset. Right.
- `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`: the `userActions` row keeps `status: live`; only its note changes. No verdict moves, and the `Spec property liveness` check is green. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: 60 success, 10 skipped (opt-in or matrix placeholders), none failed or pending. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core` and `Lint · docs & code guards` are among the green ones.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. Correct: no accept set narrows or widens and no published type changes shape.

The changeset is `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`. Both packages ship changed bytes (a description string, and the English help text generated from it), and neither changes behaviour or an accepted value, so patch is the right level for both. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: no key, type or default of the metadata protocol changes. The changeset's prose matches the diff, including its statement that the translated help texts keep their wording.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, file surface: `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts` was outside the claim. It is the generated mirror of the edited hint, and the claim amendment 7123463265 adds it. Accepted.
- Deviation, first commit made with the repo pre-commit hook skipped, then amended with hooks before any push: nothing reached the remote without the hook, and the CI lint families are green on the head. Accepted.
- Deviation, second push sent after `overlap-check` exited 1 on a generated-file conflict with #36802 in `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`: a regenerated file, outside this review's scope, and GitHub reports the PR `mergeable_state: clean` against its base. For the lane seat's ACCEPT; no contract effect.
- Deviation, one locked batch sequenced with `;`, and `test:repo` left to CI: the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here and they are green. Accepted.
- Dev flag, `check:platform-checklist` red locally on an absent symbol in files outside this diff: `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on this head, so nothing blocks this PR. The dev's out-of-scope finding stands for the seat to route.
- Dev flag, the `userActions` note's first sentence still cites the old `ListView.tsx:374`: confirmed, see N2.
- Dev flag, translated hints carry only the first sentence: confirmed, see N4.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join; it is description text.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is owed.
- The PR is a draft and no auto-merge is armed.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` — each sentence of the new describe against `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`:

1. "On by default: omitted or `true`, the renderer draws this compact toolbar; `false` draws the wide toolbar, one button per control." Holds. `:2718` is `compactToolbar: schema.compactToolbar !== false`, so `undefined` and `true` both give the compact form and only `false` gives the wide one. The test `ListView.test.tsx:1337` pins the unset case. The host forwards the key unchanged: `ui/packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:3154` passes `namedView ?? activeView ?? schema`, which is `undefined` when no one sets it, so the default is the list's own.
2. "The compact toolbar draws no Refresh button." Holds. The only Refresh button under `ui/` that reads a view key is `:8125`, `toolbarFlags.showRefresh && !toolbarFlags.compactToolbar`, `data-testid="refresh-button"` at `:8134`. `components/ViewSettingsPopover.tsx` has no occurrence of "refresh", and `displayOffered` at `:7163` does not count `showRefresh`, so Refresh is neither on the compact bar nor in the Display panel.
3. "so `userActions.refresh` governs only the wide toolbar." Holds. `userActions.refresh` has one reader under `ui/`: `:2710`, `showRefresh: ua?.refresh !== false`, and `showRefresh` has one use, `:8125`. No file under `packages/`, `apps/` or `examples/` outside the spec reads either key.
4. "pull-to-refresh is unaffected by either key." Holds. `:3680` enables `usePullToRefresh` on `!!dataSource && !!schema.objectName` alone, `handlePullRefresh` at `:3675` bumps `refreshKey` unconditionally, and `ref={pullRef}` is on the list root at `:7637`. `ui/packages/mobile/src/usePullToRefresh.ts` reads only `enabled`.

The new text also agrees with its sibling on `main`, the `userActions.refresh` describe at `view.zod.ts:1971` ("Governs only the wide toolbar's Refresh button (`compactToolbar: false`): the default toolbar has no Refresh"). The two descriptions now name each other and say the same thing from both sides. It meets the card's first Done-when clause.

Other readers of `compactToolbar` under `ui/`, each read to try to break the text:
- `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:1023, :3154`: a pass-through, no default of its own. Consistent.
- `plugin-list/src/index.tsx:236`: the registry input says "On by default; `false` draws one toolbar button per control". Consistent.
- `types/src/objectql.ts:2954`: the type is `compactToolbar?: boolean`, `@default true`. Consistent on the default; its jsdoc is stale on Refresh, see N1.
- `app-shell/.../StudioDesignSurface.tsx:5575`: the Studio Records artboard sets `compactToolbar: false` after spreading the list schema, so that one design surface draws the wide toolbar whatever the view says. See N5.
- `app-shell/.../InterfaceListPage` (census row `:519`): the interface page config has no such key, so the list's default applies. Consistent.
- The rest are tests, changelogs and key lists.

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts` — the hint is the describe verbatim, as the pin requires, so the four judgments above carry over. The neighbouring `refresh` hint at `:250` already says the same from the other side. Holds.

`packages/spec/liveness/view.json` (widened scope) — the new sentence in the `userActions` note holds: `showRefresh` is read at `:2710` and the button is drawn at `:8125` behind `!compactToolbar`, on `main` today as at the cited `5c2e34cdb`; pull-to-refresh does not read the key. It meets the card's second Done-when clause.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, none of which changes correctness or the contract on this head:
- N1 (nit) — two texts outside the diff now contradict the new describe: the jsdoc at `ui/packages/types/src/objectql.ts:2946-2953` lists Refresh among what Display carries, and `ui/packages/plugin-list/README.md:27` puts Refresh in the Display footer. Both were stale before this PR. Follow-up card.
- N2 (nit) — `view.json` keeps old objectui line numbers beside the new ones: the `userActions` note's first sentence cites `ListView.tsx:374`, and the `compactToolbar` row at `:86-89` cites `ListView.tsx:370` and `:1776-1988`. The card asked only for the `userActions.refresh` sentence. Follow-up card or accepted deviation.
- N3 (nit) — "one button per control" is the desktop reading: on the wide form the Hide fields button is `hidden sm:inline-flex` (`:7861`), so below `sm` not every control has a bar button. The Refresh button, the subject of the sentence, is drawn at every width. The wording matches the renderer's own registry text. Accepted deviation.
- N4 (nit) — the translated hints (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-zh-cn.ts:440` and the non-English bundles) keep only the first sentence, as the changeset states. Follow-up card for the translation.
- N5 (nit) — the describe says "the renderer"; the Studio Records artboard overrides the key to `false` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx:5575`). That is a design surface's own choice, not the list renderer's default, and the describe need not carry it. Accepted deviation.
- N6 (nit) — the kept first sentence still calls the panel a "View settings popover"; the UI labels it "Display". Not changed by this diff. Accepted deviation.

**VERDICT: PASS**
